Agreement between two extraction tables, field by field

Source: R/doc-extract-agreement.R
gr_extract_agreement.Rd

Compares two tables that filled one schema for the same documents: a model's gr_extract() result against a person's, or two people's. Rows are matched on the by column and each field is compared on its own, with Krippendorff's alpha at the level of measurement the field has.

Usage

gr_extract_agreement(
  x,
  y,
  fields = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  by = "document",
  B = 2000,
  conf = 0.95,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

x, y

The two tables: gr_extract() results, or data frames with a by column and one column per field. Which is the reference does not matter, since alpha and percent agreement are symmetric.

fields

Which fields to compare: a character vector of column names, a gr_fields() schema or a gr_protocol(). A schema or protocol also gives each field's type, from which its level and the way its values are read follow. NULL takes the schema of x (or y) when it is a gr_extract() result, and otherwise every column the two tables share other than by and the extraction table's bookkeeping columns.

levels

The level of measurement of each field: "nominal", "ordinal", "interval" or "ratio". A character vector named by field, or one unnamed value for every field. A field not named takes its level from its type: "interval" for integer and number fields, "nominal" for string, enum and boolean ones. An ordinal enum field is ordered as its values are declared; the ordinal level is an error for a field with no declared order (a string field, or a column with no schema that is not numeric or logical). The interval and ratio levels are an error for enum and boolean fields.

by

The column that names the document in both tables.

B, conf, seed

Bootstrap resamples for the alpha interval (0 for none), the confidence level, and the seed. The caller's random state is left as it was.

Value

An object of class gr_extract_agreement:

table

One row per field and part: field, part, level, n (documents compared), percent_agreement, alpha, lower, upper, not_reported_x, not_reported_y, unknown (matched documents left out because a cell was unknown) and note, which says why alpha is NA when it is.

pairs

Long form, one row per document and field: document, field, the two values as text (x, y) and whether each was a value, not reported or unknown (x_state, y_state). Filter it on x != y to read the disagreements.

unmatched

The documents only one table has, as a list with x and y. They are not compared.

notes, conf, bootstrap

As in hr_agreement().

Not reported

A cell that is empty, NA, or says "not reported", "not stated", "N/A" or the like is read as the document not reporting the field. In a nominal field that is one more category, so one side filling a field the other found unreported is a disagreement like any other. An ordinal, interval or ratio field cannot place "not reported" on its scale, so it gets two rows: part = "reported", the nominal agreement on whether the field is reported at all, and part = "value", the agreement on the value among the documents where both tables report it. A nominal field has the single row part = "value".

A cell is unknown, and left out of that field, when the value is there but cannot be read as the field's type ("120 (60 per arm)" in an integer field, an undeclared enum value), and in a gr_extract() result when the document was not read in full: a "failed" or "skipped" row is unknown in every field, and an empty cell of an "incomplete" row is unknown rather than not reported. A row that duplicates another document is left out, so no document counts twice. A data frame with a status column is read the same way.

How values are compared

A string value is compared after folding case, quote marks, spaces and a trailing full stop, as gr_extract() does when two parts of one document give one value two ways. Nothing else is folded, so "RCT" and "randomised controlled trial" are two values. An enum value is matched to the declared values ignoring case. Numbers are read as gr_field() describes and compared exactly, so percent agreement on a numeric field counts identical values; alpha at the interval or ratio level gives partial credit for near misses.

Alpha

Krippendorff's alpha is 1 - D_o / D_e, observed over expected disagreement computed from the coincidence matrix with the difference function of the level (Krippendorff 2011). Its interval is a percentile bootstrap over documents (Hayes and Krippendorff 2007). Alpha is reported only when at least 30 documents are compared and the field is not constant; otherwise it is NA, note says why, and percent agreement is the figure to read. Agreement between a model and a person measures how far the model's table could stand in for a person's, not which of the two is right.

References

Hayes, A. F. and Krippendorff, K. (2007). Answering the call for a standard reliability measure for coding data. Communication Methods and Measures, 1(1), 77-89.

Krippendorff, K. (2011). Computing Krippendorff's alpha-reliability. University of Pennsylvania, Annenberg School for Communication.

See also

gr_extract(), hr_agreement(), gr_fields()

Examples

fields <- gr_fields(
  design = gr_field("Study design", type = "enum",
                    values = c("rct", "cohort", "case series")),
  n      = gr_field("Number randomised", type = "integer")
)
model <- data.frame(document = c("a.pdf", "b.pdf", "c.pdf", "d.pdf"),
                    design = c("rct", "cohort", "rct", NA),
                    n = c(120, 85, NA, 40))
person <- data.frame(document = c("a.pdf", "b.pdf", "c.pdf", "d.pdf"),
                     design = c("RCT", "cohort", "rct", "case series"),
                     n = c(120, 58, NA, 40))
ag <- gr_extract_agreement(model, person, fields = fields, B = 0)
ag
#> <gr_extract_agreement> 2 field(s), 4 document(s) matched
#> 
#>   field     part    level n percent_agreement alpha lower upper not_reported_x
#>  design    value  nominal 4             0.750    NA    NA    NA              1
#>       n reported  nominal 4             1.000    NA    NA    NA              1
#>       n    value interval 3             0.667    NA    NA    NA              1
#>  not_reported_y unknown
#>               0       0
#>               1       0
#>               1       0
#> 
#> Alpha intervals at 95%; bootstrap over documents, B = 0, seed 1.
#> Note (design, value): Only 4 pairable item(s); alpha needs at least 30, so percent agreement is reported instead.
#> Note (n, reported): Only 4 pairable item(s); alpha needs at least 30, so percent agreement is reported instead.
#> Note (n, value): Only 3 pairable item(s); alpha needs at least 30, so percent agreement is reported instead.
subset(ag$pairs, x != y)
#>   document  field            x           y      x_state y_state
#> 4    d.pdf design not reported case series not reported   value
#> 6    b.pdf      n           85          58        value   value
